editorial:
You get thrown into a colorful space adventure where a cocky test pilot named Hal Jordan stumbles into a glowing green ring that turns him into a space cop. The Green Lantern Corps are basically intergalactic police, and Hal is the first human to join their ranks. The movie has a big, bright, comic-book feel with lots of CGI and a villain made of fear itself. Ryan Reynolds brings his usual charm, but the story jumps around a lot between Earth and space.

The action scenes are flashy and the suit looks cool, but the pacing feels rushed and the plot is pretty messy. Some jokes land, yet the romance and villain never fully click. If you are a die-hard DC fan or just want background noise, you might still have fun. For everyone else, it is a tough watch. You can stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent it on Apple TV, or grab the 4K Blu-ray if you are a collector.
endingExplained: In the final battle, Hal Jordan faces Parallax, the fear entity, near the sun. He lures Parallax into the sun's gravity, destroying it. Hal then returns to Earth and quits his job to fully commit to the Corps. In a mid-credits scene, Sinestro, who had been an ally, puts on a yellow ring and becomes a villain, setting up a sequel that never happened.
